column1: Meet the woman behind Anushka Sharma’s unique style
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion And why she chooses to stand out View Gallery 29 Photos Why Anushka Sharma’s style is nothing like her Bollywood contemporaries Despite her understated sense of style, Anushka Sharma frequents best dressed lists. It's safe to say, the Bollywood actor displays a quiet confidence with her wardrobe choices—be it a powerful pantsuit or a somber anarkali. More often than not, Anushka Sharma sticks to the standard fare of jeans and a jacket but she does it so well, you are bound to scan the star for style secrets. Vogue spoke to Sharma's stylist,  Allia al Rufai, on why the actor does fashion the way only a few can. What is Anushka Sharma's personal style like? I think her personal style is very cool, easy, fresh fashion. She likes taking risks every now and then. I think she stays very true to her personality in the way she dresses. She is extremely vibrant, lives in the moment and easygoing. As a stylist, how would you say you have influenced her style? My sensibility has to match with whoever I work with, that's why I work with very few clients. Somehow with Anushka, things come together very easily because her sense of style and aesthetic is very toned down; to some extent she is a minimalist. She has a good input in what she does wear and she stays true to herself which is great because she comes across as effortless. She is never doing something that doesn't resonate with her. Her sense of style does come across as understated, especially compared to her contemporaries. Is that a conscious decision? In India and Bollywood, everything is so full of colour and people do tend to overdress. If you see the way young Hollywood dresses, whether they are running errands or at a party, it's more relaxed. Here people tend to dress up a little more. For Anushka, she likes to keep things more real in that sense. But if a red-carpet event demands she dress up, she does step out in all her glory. I would say she dresses quite appropriately, given where she is and what she is attending. It's never that just because we have a pair of earrings we'll add it to the look. You will never see her over the top. She is never in excess. How do you plan outfits with Anushka? When we do promotions, which is when you will see most of her appearances, she tries to have fun with fashion as well. She is very lucky because she has such a model-esque body, she is tall and slender and can carry off pretty much any silhouette. We are always having fun, whether it's with a pair of dungarees or Indian wear with a contemporary twist to it. We do try to keep things more current rather than trendy. Does she have any favourite labels? She likes Urban Outfitters, Burberry and Dior. She tries to avoid using leather as much as she can. What's her take on Indian dressing? She likes to keep things traditional with Indian wear. We go two ways with Indian wear—either we add a contemporary touch to it, like a piece from Payal Khandwala, or we go superbly traditional with a sari or a lehenga. What's the biggest challenge you have as her stylist? We always have too many options! It's not a negative thing, but we are always deciding on picking the right look. column1: Indian designers pay poignant tributes to the late Azzedine Alaïa
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion In loving memory of the designer Azzedine Alaïa, the Tunisian-born maverick designer fondly dubbed ‘King of Cling' for his cult, curve-defining designs, passed away on Saturday morning at the age of 77. During his decades-long career, one dotted with milestones, Alaïa found favour with everyone from '90s super Naomi Campbell to former first lady Michelle Obama. Here's what the country's leading designers had to say about the industry's monumental loss. Tarun Tahiliani “I had, many years back, gone to have tea with Azzedine. He was kind, humble and puttered around his iconic studio space, organising the coffee and biscotti. He spoke no English, so we gesticulated away and chatted through mutual friends. His toiles, which he worked on with monastic fervour and discipline, were like works of art, and rather like Thierry Mugler, his jackets and bombers, fit like latex in tailoring. His glamazonian gowns had an almost museum like quality. He was a technical perfectionist. A visionary in simplicity. Beyond the boundaries of elegance.” Suneet Varma “Azzedine Alaïa may have been small in stature but he had the biggest ideas. He started the movement of bodycon dresses and was the King of Cling. Every designer from my generation watched his inspiring works and eclectic shoots in awe. His creations never got old or dated. He had the ability to make women look lithe and beautiful.” Payal Singhal “Azzedine Alaïa stood for everything that's true, honest and sincere in fashion. He always played by his own rules. He is the ultimate icon for any designer who does what he does for the pure love of fashion. When I started my career in the '90s, Alaïa had made fitted silhouettes such a huge trend. He has been a huge inspiration for me throughout my years as a fashion student and young entrepreneur. My first collection featured fitted lycra kurtas that were sexy yet classic.” Rohit Gandhi and Rahul Khanna “It was truly saddening to hear about the death of Azzedine Alaïa. The veteran couturier represented rebellious fashion. The industry has lost a man unafraid to live life his way. He went against all the odds, making the clothes that he loved, never once succumbing to trends. His perseverance and design sensibilities are fundamental factors to the current face of the fashion industry and a huge inspiration to us all.” Shantanu and Nikhil Mehra “Alaïa's untimely passing has really gripped the fashion industry by enormous sadness. We've always admired his unique approach to couture and his distinctive style will forever set his creations apart. He will be deeply missed. His carefully-guarded vision of his own personal brand and work-pace is something that has greatly inspired us. He has always followed his own timeless narratives instead of adhering to trends, and held a deep appreciation for fellow artists who did the same.” Fashion Weddings Fashion © 2019 Condé Nast

column1: Fashion industry majors join hands to fight violence against women
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Alessandro Michelle, Stella McCartney and more unite to raise awareness The Kering Foundation, part of the international luxury group Kering, has launched the #ICouldHaveBeen campaign, a new digital movement against gender-based violence in support of the International Day Against Women's Violence. As part of Kering's 6th annual White Ribbon initiative, the campaign running from November 20 to 25 sees the brand's iconic designers Alessandro Michele, Christopher Kane, Joseph Altuzarra, Dennis Chan and board directors Stella McCartney and Salma Hayek Pinault come together to stand up against gender-based violence. “Being born a girl, should not equate to a higher risk of violence. Yet, unfortunately, it is the case in our world today. We all could have been born a girl, we all must take on this combat. A combat I am proud to confront together with the Kering Foundation, our Houses and their designers via our sixth annual White Ribbon For Women campaign,” said François-Henri Pinault, chairman and CEO Kering, chairman of the Kering Foundation, in a statement. Through the ICouldHaveBeen.org website, those not born as women will be invited to enter a female name in the website, and will be made aware of the issues and violence that would have affected them had they been a woman. Similarly, women are invited to adopt HER as their first name and to encourage their family and friends to join the campaign as a show of solidarity to victims of such violence. You can see examples in the campaign visuals, which show leading male designers and personalities share what they would have been called if they were born women. There is also a collaboration in the works with influencers like Leonardo Decarli in Italy and Z.Tao in China and the Maison's creative directors, which involves a series of short films portraying the deep impact of what these young males' lives could have been had they been born a female. The campaign uses a digital platform and young influencers to target the Generation Z and millennial mindset. The focus is to raise awareness and bring about a change in the behaviour and mentality of modern young adults towards this pressing issue, which affects one out of every three girls. In light of all the gender-based issues faced by modern society, such a campaign brings in a much-needed blast of attention to provoking change. column1: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017: 8 of the biggest highlights
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Plus, all the looks from the show The 2017 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show took over Shanghai this week with special events and celebrity guests, all culminating in the brand's runway show. Every Victoria's Secret Angel walked the runway, except for the pregnant Behati Prinsloo, and the musical guests included Harry Styles, Miguel, Leslie Odom Jr., and Jane Zhang. Here, the eight must-know facts about the 2017 VS Fashion Show. Candice Swanepoel opened the show After giving birth to her son, Anacan, just over a year ago, Candice Swanepoel returned to the Victoria's Secret stage today. The South African model opened the show wearing a plaid look designed by Balmain's Olivier Rousteing complete with black and red feather wings and a studded belt. The show was divided into six sections As always, the VS show was divided into themed sections. This year, the brand opened with the “Punk Angel” group, featuring looks by Balmain, followed by a “Goddesses” section that saw models channeling Greco-Roman deities with gold laurel wreaths and ornate gold-leaf wings. (Bella Hadid fans, take note: The youngest Hadid sister walked in this section twice.) The VS Pink section was themed “Millennial Nation” and was followed by the colourful “Winter's Tale” group. The “Porcelain Angel” collection echoed the blue-and-white designs of Ming dynasty vases, and the show closed with a multicultural “Nomadic Angels” section that touched on traditions from cultures around the world. Balmain debuted its exclusive designs After months of speculation, Balmain's looks for the VS show were revealed on the runway today. Creative director Olivier Rousteing channeled a rocker spirit, showing studded, plaid, and embellished ensembles worn with Victoria's Secret x Balmain underwear that will be available in VS stores this week. In what might be a Victoria's Secret Fashion Show first, models like Stella Maxwell and Martha Hunt wore full leather jackets on the runway. Karlie Kloss returned After a three-year hiatus, Karlie Kloss returned to the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show today. Now with platinum blonde hair, Kloss walked in two sections of the show, “Punk Angels” and “Winter's Tale,” taking turns in a red tartan cape and a silvery jacket with blue flower wings. Alessandra Ambrosio walked her last show ever . . . maybe Rumours are swirling that Alessandra Ambrosio will retire her angel wings this year. The veteran model, who's walked in 17 consecutive Victoria's Secret shows, took two runway passes this year, dressed in a punk outfit by Balmain and a “Nomadic Angels” look that featured enormous feathered wings. During her last runway walk, she blew a big kiss to the audience, a gesture some have interpreted as her goodbye. Harry Styles opted for monochrome suiting Expecting some floral suiting from Harry Styles? Think again. The pop star wore two monochrome suits for his VS Fashion Show performance. The first was a black double-breasted Gucci suit with velvet trim that he paired with a very-appropriate pink shirt. Afterwards he changed into a pale mint suit by Givenchy by Clare Waight Keller with a matching shirt. The Pink Section got even more athleisure-y Accompanied by Chinese pop star Jane Zhang and a cabal of backup dancers, the Pink models strutted out in tiny puffer jackets and track pants in bright colours—not just pink! For the second year in a row, Grace Elizabeth opened that section, this time wearing an inflatable letter P like a backpack. Lais Ribeiro killed it in the fantasy bra Where else does a gold leaf and sapphire-adorned Fantasy Bra belong than in the “Goddesses” section? Lais Ribeiro wore the out-of-this-world number with a laurel wreath crown. column1: Longines celebrates 185 years at Beijing’s Imperial Ancestral Temple
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Here’s everything you need to know View Gallery 9 Photos Longines celebrated its 185th anniversary in the Ancient Imperial Temple in Beijing To talk about a brand's journey for nearly two centuries warrants a historic setting to narrate the tale against. Swiss watchmakers Longines perfected this when they celebrated their 185th anniversary and the launch of the record collection at the Tai Miao or the Imperial Ancestral Temple in Beijing. Walking into the historic site late in the evening as it's lit up on either side, gives you goosebumps and not just because of the merciless wind in the Chinese capital. If the exteriors of the setting signify tradition, the anniversary party was all about being with the times. Easily one of the best performing markets in the world for Longines, China was the obvious destination to host the milestone moment. Joining the ranks of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Kate Winslet and Simon Baker, Zhao Liying was announced as the Longines Ambassador of Elegance. One of the most widely recogniszed faces in Chinese cinema, Liying also made it to number four on the Forbes' 2017 Top 100 Chinese Celebrities list. Those who followed the happenings at Baselworld 2017 might already be aware of the Record Collection launched by Longines. Exemplifying the brand's penchant for minimalist, elegant and classic aesthetic, the Record Collection is culmination of what fans of Longines love the most about their watches. “Tradition, elegance and performance, three values dear to Longines, are perfectly combined in the new collection that we are launching today: the Record Collection. Indeed, its models do not simply show Longines' watchmaking expertise, but they are also a display of the brand's signature classic style,” said Walter von Känel, president of Longines. The Record Collection has been given a “chronometer” distinction by the Swiss Official Chronometer Testing Institute. Watch fans will be pleased to know that each of timepieces boast of a single-crystal silicon balance spring making them immune to inconsistency in performance. The collection was later displayed at the Anniversary Exhibition hosted in the Tai Miao with other iconic timepieces from the Longines history. The evening also marked the launch of the ‘Longines through Time' a historical book, written by Stéphanie Lachat, Longines International brand heritage manager that charts the history of the brand. Arriving on the red carpet with parents Sridevi and Boney Kapoor, the upcoming actor opted for an applique choli and a lehenga skirt-pants hybrid featuring embroidered detail by Anamika Khanna for the event. Another unusual element of her outfit was the lehenga-pants hybrid—the slim pants had a connected skirt over it, adding visual drama to her red carpet look. Kapoor anchored her busy separates with a black and white embroidered clutch by The Pink Potli, drop earrings by Shree Pramani Jewels and classic black heels. Keeping her beauty look simple, she went with sleek eyeliner, peachy lips, dewy make-up and messy curls. column1: Bridal wear shopping guide: Best designers, jewellers and more in Kolkata
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Hit the right spots Kolkata—the land of the intellectual and the offbeat, a city that heavily steeped in old world charm is known for its unique viewpoint. Culturally and fashion-wise, this makes for a great shopping hub, as you are bound to find treasures for your wedding trousseau that are unlikely to be found anywhere. Here's a comprehensive guide to finding everything you need before your big day. View Gallery 7 Photos Where to shop for a wedding in Kolkata – Designers Presenting more of a local flavour as well as promoting some known names from the fashion space are two additional stores in Kolkata worth a visit: Vachi (Tel: 033-24540975), where one may find selections that include Rohit Bal and Gaurav Gupta. Zenon (Tel: 033-40675204), where AM:PM, Anju Modi and Pallavi Mohan have stocked their collections. View Gallery 4 Photos Where to shop for a wedding in Kolkata – Jewellery Kolkata takes pride in its heritage of traditional jewellery and there's so much to choose from if you're looking to take a slice of Bengal back with you. The intricate ‘Ratanchur', more commonly known as the haathphool, can be found in a five-finger style, sporting motifs like the sun, moon and lotus. ‘Balas' and ‘Kaan Balas' are bangles and earrings respectively, in typical Bengali motifs. ‘Chik' is the customary gold choker worn at many weddings along with a more ornate ‘Paati Haar'. Even the ‘Tikli', or maang tikka, is peculiar to the style of its region. Where can you find these local gems? Head to PC Chandra (Pcchandraindia.com; Tel: 033-22231279) and Anjali Jewellers (Anjalijewellers.in; Tel: 033-24455785) A common thread unites the stores mentioned in this section; they all follow principles of sustainable and thoughtful fashion and integrate their units to support craft, artisans, natural fibres and hand weaves. View Gallery 4 Photos Where to shop for a wedding in Kolkata – Fabric and sari stores If you're willing to go the distance, then a visit to the Phulia region a couple of hours drive from Kolkata, won't disappoint. The silk here is spun via a unique weaving process and a lot of export production for international houses takes place here. If fabric in bulk is on your must-buy list, then do add Amulya Basak or any of the other big stores in the area to your itinerary. column1: This new Mumbai restaurant will feature a fashion runway inside it
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion A new offering from the people behind PizzaExpress How do you make a pizza parlour with a mass appeal offer a curated, local experience? Ramit Mittal and Deepinder Batth of Gourmet Investments, the group behind the popular restaurant chain PizzaExpress in India have already been working towards personalising dining for its patrons. Their unique solution to the conundrum lies in the ‘The Project Series' which offers patrons of different localities, specialised experiences that set the space apart from the rest. After offering Mumbai The Bandra Project by PizzaExpress earlier this year, the city will get its second such restaurant—The Runway Project by PizzaExpress in High Street Phoenix in Lower Parel this month. Fashion first To launch The Runway Project, Mittal and Batth have called upon the OGs of the fashion scene in India. Veteran designer Hemant Trivedi, the man behind the pageant gowns for the likes of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Priyanka Chopra, Lara Dutta and more will be hosting the launch party. “I am feeling honoured The Runway Project can actually value and pay tribute to one of the oldest players in India's 40 years of fashionable growth,” said Trivedi. The launch event will be expecting a star-studded guest list including Aishwarya Rai Bachchan. “I am truly looking forward to sharing a very precious evening with my very valued friends from the industry and celebrate an exciting extension of fashionable nouvelle cuisine as well,” the designer added. The space will not only have its own runway (obviously) but also have a members-only lounge called ‘The Gold Leaf' hidden behind a curtain. Safe to say, The Runway Project will not only serve as a space for designers to showcase their work but also a space to host parties and events. Makeover story "We are committed to creating spaces that are more than just restaurants and bars, but are addresses that are hyper local, while always being about curated experiences and settings that stimulate conversations” says Mittal, CEO, Gourmet Investments Ltd. Anand Basrai of the Busride Design Studio, also behind The Bandra Project will be lending his design aesthetic to the space. Think vintage dressing rooms, 3-D wall murals, a whole load of whimsy and seasonal change in the façade every three months. Extra toppings Not unlike the specialised cocktails and menu at other from The Project Series, the bar at The Runway Project promises to be hip and current meanwhile, celebrity chef Vicky Ratnani will be adding his own flair to the food menu. PizzaExpress will opening other such localised restaurants in Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai, Pune, and Delhi and Gurgaon in the next 12 months. “Each of our openings in India will be a communal hub of sorts known for great hospitality, distinctive design, whimsical decor and memorable times," Deepinder Batth, COO, Gourmet Investments Ltd. column1: 6 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show stars remember the first show 22 years later
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Flashback View Gallery 11 Photos 6 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show stars remember the first show 22 years later In 1995, a mid-market lingerie brand headquartered in Ohio decided to host a fashion show. Staged in New York's plush Plaza Hotel, some of the biggest supermodels of the time—Stephanie Seymour, Veronica Webb and Beverly Peele—were recruited to walk. Models wore modest bias-cut slips, cheongsams and bralettes on the runway, accessorised with cardigans, prim handbags and plaid dressing gowns—wearable, yes, but lacking a certain razzle-dazzle. There were no TV cameras, no music performances, and certainly no wings. Some model castings were done over the phone. A few hundred people saw it, and virtually none of the journalists in the room chose to cover it. Fast-forward 22 years and the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show has changed almost beyond recognition. The TV broadcast is watched by a global audience of millions, accompanied by live performances from the world's biggest pop stars—Taylor Swift and The Weeknd among them. Models undergo months of rigorous training, donning expensive, elaborately constructed outfits that can weigh upwards of 30 pounds. But the first show, masterminded by Victoria's Secret executives Ed Razek and Monica Mitro, gave a glimpse of what the modern fashion show was to become. Celebrities—including Donald Trump and Russell Simmons—dotted the front row at a time when the prime seats were reserved solely for editors and models dominated the covers of magazines. Victoria's Secret understood the power of celebrity in fashion well before the fashion industry itself did. Below, six attendees of the original Victoria's Secret Fashion Show tell us what it was like. Catherine McCord Then: Model Now: Chef and entrepreneur “I remember the fittings, Ed [Razek] was there and so was Monica [Mitro]. I was totally nervous—oh my God! You forget that back then it was all about print, and the Victoria's Secret catalogue was everything. Back then, you were either a runway and magazine model, or you were catalogue, but somehow Victoria's Secret was able to break that boundary. I don't think the show prep was intense in the way it is now, but I do remember doing lymphatic drainage, and having lots of leg massages. It's comical when you look back at the photos—we were almost fully dressed. There were cardigans! Even so, I did feel scantily clad. I'd done shows in London, Milan and Paris, but I remember getting to the end of the runway and suddenly feeling self-conscious because the atmosphere was different. It was more a mix of normal people and journalists. I'm sure I remember seeing Donald Trump in the audience. Models didn't have publicists, we were just throwing off our clothes, we were naked—I'm on the more conservative side, and I don't think any of us thought twice about it.” Ron Galella Then: Paparazzo Now: Retired “I didn't pay much attention to the audience—I couldn't stop looking at the models. The models were the heroines. I know some of the models were nervous, but they never showed it, they were so graceful on the runway. Today they go overboard with the costumes; they have wings, they have gimmicks. In 1995 they didn't have all that: the models were the main event. I think that something got lost; to me the first show was best. If you have Stephanie Seymour on the runway, what more do you need?” Veronica Webb Then: Model Now: Model, writer and founder of Webb On The Fly “I was lucky, my casting was a phone call from my agency saying, ‘Go to your fitting for the show'. [Victoria's Secret executive vice president] Monica Mitro is one of the nicest people you'll ever want to meet and she supervised every fitting personally. I had this white corset with white stockings and suspenders and white high heels. I think I did nearly 1,000 squats the week before and went on a ketogenic diet to reduce bloat. You're in your underwear so it's all about your body and how strong and healthy you are—there's nowhere to hide a single body flaw. It was a great exercise in overcoming fear and self-consciousness. But it is a show like no other. It was a big, glam pyjama party with all your besties sharing the spotlight.” Gail Elliott Then: Model Now: Designer and founder, Little Joe Woman by Gail Elliott “I walked thousands of runways for 24 years and the two I remember are the first Victoria's Secret show and Gianni Versace's ‘Freedom' show. Back then, backstage was almost as exciting as the shows. Champagne would be flowing and all the models' boyfriends—who were actors, movie stars, rock stars, musicians and screenwriters—were photographed having fun. I don't remember it being stressful or feeling nervous, although I guess doing a show in my underwear should have been. I probably wore less clothing at Versace shows! During the show there were a lot of wolf whistles from the audience. The audience wasn't there to buy: Victoria's Secret's vision for the show was different and they've certainly kept it up today with the Angels, pink planes and mega hype. It's a clever company.” Holly Brubach Then: Style editor, New York Times Magazine Now: Author and screenwriter “I have only the dimmest memory of that first show at the Plaza. It doesn't surprise me that there wasn't much coverage back then. I do recall that most members of the fashion press regarded it as not ‘legitimate' in terms of design and trends, more of a mall brand. Which it was. But I thought it was such an interesting phenomenon, and I'm not surprised that it has been such a big media success. I think of it as being in the same category as the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue—something that gets a lot of attention and builds a ‘halo' around the brand. The product is sort of beside the point.” Ingrid Seynhaeve Then: Model Now: Founder of June 7.2 “I was very proud to be opening the show. It was quite nerve-wracking, as we were in lingerie and I was used to the couture and high fashion shows like Valentino, Ralph Lauren and Dior. You have to walk in a sexy way, playing with the camera, feeling—and looking—like a million dollars with not much on. But it was a fun change to have eye contact with the public and cameras, and to make a statement at the end of the runway. The show grew bigger and bigger each year, I think I must have walked the show five times. It helped with our day rates and became the most prestigious show to do. It gave me a voice as a model afterwards as so many people saw me in interviews on TV.” What's New Fashion Culture & Living © 2019 Condé Nast

column1: Masaba Gupta unveils her first cruise line on board an actual cruise boat
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Here’s your first look View Gallery 4 Photos Masaba Gupta unveils her first cruise line on board an actual cruise boat Close on the heels of the launch of her maiden line of timepieces with Titan Raga, the one-woman army that is Masaba Gupta has already moved on to the next agenda on her bursting calendar—her first-ever cruise collection in association with Lexus. The auto company launched their latest hybrid electric car, the NX300h, alongside Gupta's line. Marking another first was the fact that this was also the designer's first off-site show. Forgoing the predictability of the mandatory hotel ballroom, guests were invited to hop aboard Mumbai's only floating restaurant, AB Celestial, last night, with the Mumbai skyline serving as a glittering backdrop for the double showcase. Cruise life The idea for the collection was born from the need to create a holiday line that was easy to travel with and could easily complement the wearer's existing wardrobe. “While the concept of cruise collections is more international, it is the increase in travel amongst urban Indians that makes this collection relevant,” explains Gupta. “People are taking more breaks and exploring newer destinations. Women are no longer content with simply throwing in what they already own into the suitcase. Holiday looks are being taken very seriously.” Right on cue, the well-thought-out separates from this capsule collection are designed for versatile mixing-and-matching. Kaftans, maxis and swimwear cover-ups that are easy to accessorise are a highlight. The underlying vibe is tropical, but the pieces are deliberately trans-seasonal in nature. “Careful thought has gone into every outfit. For instance, the denim sari cover up is perfect for drinks right after lounging in the pool. The jacket is easy to throw on but the drape has been added for when one does not want to reveal too much décolletage at the bar.” Weddings galore The collection also boasts a festive leg that is high on destination wedding suitability. “I pretty much made this collection to address my own wardrobe needs!” she laughs. After attending a wedding in Thailand recently, the designer realised that curating looks for destination weddings always turns out to be a demanding process. So she took it upon herself to create fuss-free wedding wear that you can simply throw into your bag without having to worry about luggage allowances. Pieces like the off-shoulder cape paired with a patterned skirt, silk jacket with a three-meter skirt hem, and cold shoulder tasseled kaftan are ideal for those with zero affinity for two-kilo lehengas. “The foil print shirt and pant set can easily be worn with a necklace for a sundowner or pool party. I think the dupatta is now irrelevant, so there are also printed lehenga sets that do away with it.” The collaboration “The venue for the show was Lexus' idea—the idea was to disrupt clichés in every possible away. AB Celestial gave us enough space for the show and car launch as well as a party area,” said the designer of working with Lexus. Not one to mince words, Gupta makes no bones about calling out hotel ballrooms as a redundant way of hosting showcases. “It's bad enough that we have to resort to them at fashion week. But such locations don't add to the clothes in any way, and there is nothing unexpected or exciting about them. The idea is curate an experience for your invitees, just like shows by international brands where venues are chosen to uplift the theme of the collection. I will only do off-site shows in the future.” Zooming ahead Lexus' latest offering, the NX300h, will be available in two models, F Sport and Luxury, and is targeted at an environmentally conscious, urban, influential set. “The luxurious new Lexus NX300h is all about what an automobile could be—breathtakingly striking from every angle and unique in its personality. This is a vehicle crafted for the urban sophisticate who is arriving—in signature style,” said Akitoshi Takemura, president, Lexus India, on the occasion of the launch. column1: Fashion world mourns the death of Azzedine Alaïa
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion The revered fashion designer was 77 The Tunisian-born couturier Azzedine Alaïa has died in Paris at the age of 77. The Sphinx-like designer, once dubbed "the King of Cling", was highly revered for his garments that moulded the body into extraordinary proportions, the product of an obsessive craftsman who bears more resemblance to a sculptor than a fashion designer. "Azzedine Alaïa was a true visionary, and a remarkable man. He will be deeply missed by all of those who knew and loved him, as well as by the women around the world who wore his clothes," said Vogue editor-in-chief Edward Enninful this morning. "The generosity of his spirit and genius of his designs will never be forgotten." Born in Tunis on February 26,  1940 to wheat farmers, Alaïa was an early devotee to Vogue and cheated his way into the local Institut Supérieur des Beaux Arts in Tunis to study sculpture. He noted that "when I realised I couldn't be an amazing sculptor, I changed direction" - segueing into fashion. He began assisting a dress-maker and, having built up a private client base, he moved to Paris in 1957. He soon got a job at Christian Dior, in the midst of the Algerian war, but was dismissed for having incorrect immigration papers. From Dior he went to Guy Laroche, where he spent two seasons, then to Thierry Mugler, but a series of high-society patrons allowed him to set up his own workshop. Elegant swans such as the Comtesse of Blegiers offered him lodgings in exchange for dress-making and babysitting. Hollywood stars such as Greta Garbo and the Seventies jet-set, which included Marie-Hélène de Rothschild, came regularly for fittings. He produced his first ready-to-wear collection in 1980, in conjunction with a move to a studio in the Marais. It was a smash hit: moulded in leather, it was as erotically charged as it was ground-breaking. Over the years he continued to create collections to the beat of his own drum, eschewing the traditional seasonal calendars, from which he retired in 1992: “When the collection is ready, it's ready,” was Alaïa's attitude. He showed a surprise couture collection in July, his first since 2011, in which Naomi Campbell made a rare catwalk appearance to rapturous reviews. column1: Here’s where to go for Bollywood-inspired ethnic wear
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Silks and more View Gallery 6 Photos A new Bollywood-inspired ethnicwear collection comes to town Whether it's the character, the set or the plot line, designers are constantly turning to cinema for fashion inspiration. With an entire collection dedicated to Vidya Balan's upcoming comedy-drama Tumhari Sulu, Mumbai-based designer label Gopi Vaid by Gopi and Arnaz is the newest to join the party. You've probably chanced upon her store in Kala Ghoda, which she runs with her partner Arnaz Soonawala, or noticed her designs at stores like Aza, Ogaan and Elahe. It all started when the Tumhari Sulu crew took over Vaid's workshop, transforming her Lower Parel design studio into an industrial unit for the film's set. Instead of taking the constant presence of a Bollywood film crew in her working space as an inconvenience, Vaid looked at it as an opportunity for inspiration.“I loved the aesthetics of the movie. I loved the detailing that went through in doing the whole set. I really enjoyed the whole theme. That's why I felt like I wanted to create something.” Just like that, Vaid dared to dedicate her time working on an entire collection inspired by the movie's prime character Sulu, whom she describes as a vivacious, fun-loving and friendly woman with an attitude she could identify with. “Sulu is just a very real, bold Indian girl who doesn't take no for an answer. She wants to live life to the most. And these saris are full of life,” the designer continues. Having given up working with the chiffon fabric on saris after she felt they would not do well commercially, Vaid decided to give the fabric another try with the collection. The limited-edition line includes about 25 saris, lehengas and tunics with similar prints between the price range of Rs 15,500 to Rs 23,500 and boasts of chintz prints, gota patti, organza. The focus is to grasp the attention of a younger audience and make the printed chiffon sari a must-have in their wardrobes while also keeping in mind the needs of a mature audience's wardrobes. “It's for someone who loves life and wants to do something different. I think you need to feel young. Everybody has that daring personality inside them. You just have to give it life,” Vaid tells us. The label officially launched their saris with a special promotional event held at their Kala Ghoda store with guests including Vidya Balan, who wore a dark green sari from the collection. For Vaid, her admiration for Sulu extends to a wider appreciation she feels towards Vidya Balan, whom she finds relatable and filled with a youthful energy. Her interactions with Balan on set played a big role in drawing her towards designing the collection. In fact, the use of chiffon saris in her collection was influenced by Balan, who enjoys wearing them off-screen as well. Fashion Fashion Culture & Living © 2019 Condé Nast

column1: Can you wear sheer clothing in your 40s?
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Or more to the point, why can’t you? View Gallery 12 Photos Can you wear sheer clothing in your 40s? The forties can seem like a daunting era for your wardrobe. You definitely don't want to be caught in the relics from your early 20s, but do you absolutely have to break up with your favourite sheer LBD? The answer to that would be a yes and a no—with two decades of professional dressing experience behind you as a bona fide adult, you've worked on honing your style, and the forties needn't warrant a seismic shift to a boring aesthetic. Any trend is only as good as how you work it into your individual style, and no, just because you've hit the big four-oh, you needn't swear off the runway favourites altogether. Sheer has taken over our collective fashion conscience, cropping up everywhere from the closets of street style stars to showbiz veterans. Once relegated to sexy negligees, this risqué trend has stepped out of the bedroom to make space for itself in the party section of your wardrobe as well as the workwear section the next morning. Wondering how to work the trend without risking any OTT moments? Take notes from the best. Starry inspiration If you're looking for proof that age is just a set of digits, look to Malaika Arora whose wardrobe is only becoming more defined in her 40s. From nailing easy chic with a belted sheer tunic to showing off her curves in a traffic-stopping Manish Malhotra mini, there's little that does without any flair. Likewise, Karisma Kapoor loves to play up her collarbones with sheer necklines, while Shilpa Shetty Kundra has the last word on nifty layering–if you're running out of outfit ideas for brunch, look to her belted floral tunic over printed separates from Arpita Mehta. What you should do Not quite sure where to begin? Take a call on how comfortable you are, start from there and slowly work your way up. If you aren't at your most confident with see-through fabrics, simply layer a sheer blouse with an opaque suit at work. Once you've built that essential base of trust, try layering a mesh sheer top under a jumpsuit or play with proportions by throwing on a diaphanous frock over a body con dress. Off-duty day out with the girls? Shrug on a see-through midi dress over your favourite bralette and ripped denim. If you're looking to make things fun, invest in one sheer wardrobe staple and challenge yourself to find different ways to style it without ever repeating a look.  Chances are you won't run out of options before fall is over. What you definitely shouldn't do While the very nature of sheer clothing calls for some fashion adventures, anything that your teenaged self thinks cool will definitely serve as a red flag. Depending on the occasion you're dressing for, ensure that you stay on the right side of risqué yet experimental. The occasional peekaboo flash of skin might keep things interesting, but you don't want to get called in by HR. An easy copout would be to incorporate sheer elements into your already existing workwear wardrobe, and reserve the sheer LBDs and playsuits for weekends. This adventurous fabric also calls for military precision when picking the innerwear that goes along with it. An ill-fitting bralette will land you in the doghouse, as will jarring prints. While shopping, mentally picture the innerwear that would go along with it. If you're drawing a blank, don't expect to wing it later on, but instead make a detour to the lingerie aisle for some new additions. All set? Pick from our edit of the most fun sheer styles on the market right now. column1: Deepika Padukone channels three very different looks in less than 24 hours
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Girl on the go View Gallery 5 Photos Deepika Padukone steps out in 3 versatile outfits for Padmavati promotions Deepika Padukone's schedule is slowly getting packed with Padmavati promotions as we move closer to its release date. Yesterday, the actor was spotted going through three outfit changes—a one-shoulder top and trousers by Prabal Gurung, a kurta and sharara set by Rimple and Harpreet Narula, and a dress by Bibhu Mohapatra. If we could pick one winning look from yesterday, it would be the coral red off-shoulder dress by Bibhu Mohapatra. The ruffled sleeves and the the extended trail of her ensemble added drama to the embellishment-free look, while the black bodice offered an arresting visual contrast. The actor accentuated the voluminous outfit with nothing but sleek drop earrings by Eina Ahluwalia and black tie-up heels. The actor went with a pulled-back messy bun to leave the focus on her dress and added a burgundy lip colour and mascara in the mix. With party season looming, those with a red carpet event or black tie gala on the calendar should take a page from Padukone's playbook and invest in a dramatically voluminous number. column1: Liu Wen: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Name: Liu Wen Age: 29 Nationality: Chinese Height: 5'10'' VS shows to date: 5 Born in Yongzhou, a small village in the southern Chinese province of Hunan, Liu Wen is China's first global supermodel. Liu has had a career of firsts. In 2009, she became the first Chinese model to walk the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show. A year later, she became the first Asian global spokesmodel for cosmetics giant Estée Lauder. The work has paid off: In 2013, she became the first Asian model to appear on Forbes' highest-paid models list. View Gallery 3 Photos Liu Wen: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile Liun began her modelling career after winning the reality TV competition, New Silk Road World Model Contest, in 2005. She moved from her hometown to Beijing, and started working with the Chinese editions of Vogue and Harper's Bazaar. For the autumn/winter 2010 season, she walked an impressive 74 shows, and was the second most-booked catwalk model for spring/summer 2010, with 70 shows. As an Estée Lauder global ambassador, Liu has spoken out about beauty stereotypes and has challenged traditional ideals of beauty. “I don't know if I can ever truly represent what ‘beautiful' means in my native culture,” she told Vogue, “but I hope that in both China and beyond, I can help more people understand how a definition of beauty can encompass more elements than ever before.” Liu practices spinning and hot yoga, and likes to stretch every day. For breakfast, she alternates between traditional Chinese congee, and Western oatmeal with soy milk and raisins. column1: Taylor Hill: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Name: Taylor Hill Age: 21 Nationality: American Height: 5'9'' VS shows to date: 3 Taylor Hill was training as a gymnast when she was discovered in 2011 on a ranch in Granby, Colorado, by photographer and agent Jim Jordan. The young model signed with IMG and started landing jobs before turning 15. She made her international debut three years later during New York Fashion Week, walking for DKNY, 3.1 Phillip Lim and Ralph Lauren. Since then, Hill has walked for Chanel, Balmain and Versace; become a face of Lancome; and, more recently, designed four collection for the denim brand Joe's Jeans. View Gallery 2 Photos Taylor Hill: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile Hill walked her first VS fashion show in 2014, shortly after her 18th birthday. With 9.2 million followers on Instagram, she is among the 20 most-followed models in the world, but despite her obvious good looks, Hill claims she wasn't the most popular girl in high school. “I was really shy because I was so tall and I had bad posture and was like ‘Hey guys!'” the model told Vogue. “Then I started modelling and all of these people who didn't talk to me started messaging me on Facebook, like, ‘Hey remember me?' I thought, ‘Yeah, I remember how mean you were to me!'” Hill is part of a fashion family: her sister Mackinley and her brother Chase are also signed to IMG, while her oldest sister Logan Rae is a photographer. She currently lives in New York City with her boyfriend, actor and former model Michael Stephen Shank. Hill thinks Angelina Jolie is the most beautiful woman in the world, loves Hot Cheetos chips and Swedish Fish, and travels with a bag of instant oatmeal in her purse. Her workout regimen includes CrossFit, cross-training and weight training, which she balances out with a bit of yoga. column1: Jasmine Tookes: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Name: Jasmine Tookes Age: 26 Nationality: American Height: 5'9'' VS shows to date: 5 Born and raised in Huntington Beach, California, Jasmine Tookes was equally into sports and fashion at a young age. She played volleyball and softball, and practiced gymnastics, and when not working out, accompanied her celebrity stylist mother on set. It was at one of her mother's showroom appointments that Tookes, aged 16, was officially discovered, although at the time she had already starred in an Abercrombie & Fitch advertising campaign shot by Bruce Weber. Tookes booked campaigns with Gap, Ugg and DKNY in 2010, but her big break happened in September 2011, when she walked for Prada, Versace and Salvatore Ferragamo during Milan Fashion Week. A year later, in 2012, she debuted on the Victoria's Secret runway and has been an Angel since 2015. View Gallery 3 Photos Jasmine Tookes: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 In 2016, she became the first woman of colour to wear the brand's Fantasy Bra in nearly a decade, following Tyra Banks in 2007. The same year, Tookes debuted on Forbes' highest-paid models list. To stay fit, Tookes mixes barre corre, pilates, weight training and yoga, staying motivated by signing up to classes with her Angel friends. She shares a fitness Instagram account with fellow Angel Josephine Skriver, and indulges in pizza and hot wings on occasion. column1: Stella Maxwell: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Name: Stella Maxwell Age: 27 Nationality: British and Irish Height: 5'9'' VS shows to date: 3 Stella Maxwell had an extraordinarily international upbringing. Born in Belgium to Northern Irish parents, she spent a year in Australia at the age of 13, before settling in Wellington, New Zealand, a year later. While studying at the University of Otago in New Zealand, a hairdresser suggested she try modelling, so she went to see Aliana McDaniel, then owner of a local modelling agency. She was signed instantly and soon moved to Paris. View Gallery 3 Photos Stella Maxwell: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile In 2009, Maxwell landed her first international jobs, including an appearance in the October issue of British Vogue shot by Mario Testino, a lookbook campaign for Alexander McQueen, and shows for Fashion East and Luella at London Fashion Week. More recently, she has walked for Chanel, Jeremy Scott, Versace, Balmain and Philipp Plein, and has been on the cover of Vogue Brasil, Turkey, Germany and Spain. Maxwell walked her first Victoria's Secret show in 2014 and was made an Angel a year later. She is currently the only Brit with an Angel contract. In 2016, Maxwell joined Max Factor as a global brand ambassador. Her most recent campaigns include Jeremy Scott, Roberto Cavalli Eyewear and Topshop. Beyond modelling, Maxwell has been in the spotlight because of her love life. In 2015, she was reportedly dating singer Miley Cyrus, and although neither of them has ever confirmed the relationship, Cyrus's 2017 song "She's Not Him" is rumored to be about Maxwell. The model is currently in another high-profile relationship, this time with actress Kristen Stewart. Her pre-show prep includes getting as much sleep as possible, eating clean and drinking lots of water. She is very serious about her yoga practice, often filming her moves with her phone to track her progress. Gluten-free toast with avocado is one of her favourite treats, and she's in love with Trip, a Chihuahua mix she found on the street and adopted with Stewart. column1: Alessandra Ambrosio: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Name: Alessandra Ambrosio Age: 36 Nationality: Brazilian Height: 5'10'' VS shows to date: 16 Born in the Brazilian town of Erechim, Alessandra Ambrosio developed an interest in modelling at a young age, enrolling for modelling classes when she was 12 years old. She broke into the international scene in the late ‘90s, after being selected as one of the finalists of the 1996 edition of the Elite Model Look competition. Soon, she was booked for the Millennium Guess Campaign, and has since appeared on more than 70 magazine covers, including Vogue Spain, Brazil, Germany and Mexico. View Gallery 3 Photos Alessandra Ambrosio: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile In 2000, Ambrosio made her debut on the Victoria's Secret runway and became an Angel four years later. She is one of the longest-serving Angels, together with Adriana Lima. “When I first did my show in 2000, I remember that all the outfits were very, very small,” she told Vogue. “There were barely any wings, compared to what you see now.” In 2005, in one of her most famous VS appearances, she wore lingerie made of candy. In 2003, Ambrosio was featured in the Pirelli Calendar and over the years has appeared in a number of TV shows and films, including Casino Royale, Entourage, New Girl and How I Met Your Mother. She has been engaged to businessman Jamie Mazur since 2008, when she gave birth to their first daughter, Anja. The same year, the model made headlines by returning to the VS catwalk only three months after giving birth. Their second child, Noah, was born in 2012, when Ambrosio was chosen to wear the Floral Fantasy bra, created by Long Island's London Jewelers. Ambrosio loves sports, including swimming and volleyball, and practices Pilates, barre and yoga. She maintains a balanced diet throughout the year, but can't resist eating cupcakes with her two children, and the occasional glass of red wine at dinner. column1: Sara Sampaio: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Name: Sara Sampaio Age: 26 Nationality: Portuguese Height: 5'8'' VS shows to date: 4 Born in Porto, Portugal, Sara Sampaio was discovered at the age of 15. A year later, in 2007, she won the Cabelos Pantene hair modelling contest to appear in an advertisement for the brand. Despite her early success, Sampaio made sure to finish her high school studies before embarking on a professional modelling career, which she began while studying part-time at the University of Lisbon. Sampaio's breakthrough came at the end of 2011, when she appeared for the first time on the cover of Vogue Portugal. She has been the face of Italian brand Calzedonia from 2012 to 2015; has walked for Dolce & Gabbana, Elie Saab and Miu Miu; and was the first Portuguese model to be featured in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue, winning her a spot on Models.com's Top Sexiest Models. View Gallery 3 Photos Sara Sampaio: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile In 2013, she finally debuted on the VS catwalk, after being turned away in 2011 and 2012. “The third time I thought, ‘I'm not giving them any excuse not to pick me',” she told Vogue. “This is a very special booking, you have to earn your way into it.” In 2015, she became an Angel. Sampaio campaigns against animal cruelty, supporting the American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals, and has a long-haired chihuahua called Luigi Sampaio. She dreams of having a house full of dogs. To stay in shape she practices SLT (strengthen, lengthen and tone), a hybrid pilates workout, and goes for the occasional run. She suggests always working out with a partner to keep the motivation high and planking as the best way to get killer abs. She's partial to pancakes, banana and strawberry smoothies, Skittles and carbs in general. column1: Behati Prinsloo: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Name: Behati Prinsloo Age: 28 Nationality: Namibian Height: 5'10'' VS shows to date: 9 Born in South Africa, Behati Prinsloo grew up in Grootfontein, a small town in Namibia. An only child, Prinsloo was an active kid, spending much of her time outdoors and practicing gymnastics, track, riding and field hockey. She was first spotted while vacationing in Cape Town with her grandparents, and soon after left Grootfontein Secondary School to move to London and pursue a career in modelling. She debuted on the Milan catwalks for spring/summer 2006 as an exclusive for Prada and Miu Miu and the following season worked with Supreme, Marc Jacobs and Narciso Rodriguez. That same year, she starred in her first two international campaigns with Nina Ricci and Aquascutum. A year later, she was featured on her first Vogue cover and debuted on the Victoria's Secret catwalk. Prinsloo has been walking for the lingerie brand every year from 2007 to 2015, becoming an Angel in 2009. She has opened the show twice, in 2014 and 2015. View Gallery 3 Photos Behati Prinsloo: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile In 2010, she added designer to her CV, launching a swimwear collection for Victoria's Secret Pink, and in 2016, she designed a line with Juicy Couture. In 2014, Prinsloo married Maroon 5 singer Adam Levine, giving birth to their first baby, Dusty Rose, in 2016. In September 2017, Prinsloo and Levine announced their second pregnancy. Prinsloo exercises three to four times per week, and is devoted to a dance-cardio routine called Body by Simone, as well as yoga and stretching. Breakfast is her favourite meal—especially when it involves eggs and avocado on toast. column1: Candice Swanepoel: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Name: Candice Swanepoel Age: 29 Nationality: South African Height: 5'9'' VS shows to date: 9 Candice Swanepoel grew up on a dairy and beef farm in Mooi River, South Africa, rising regularly at dawn to help her father milk the cows. The hard-working attitude has stayed with her—she still wakes up at 5 a.m. most days, be it for a shoot or for a full-body workout that includes yoga, boxing, pilates and resistance training. She has often described her teen self as awkward-looking and didn't envision a career in modelling until she was scouted, aged 15, at a flea market. When Victoria's Secret got in touch with Swanepoel's agent in 2007, she had been thinking about quitting modelling, because of the loneliness of the trade. Luckily, she found herself at home among the Angels, becoming close friends with fellow South African Behati Prinsloo, as well as Lily Aldridge and Rosie Huntington-Whiteley. View Gallery 3 Photos Candice Swanepoel: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile Swanepoel's relationship with VS catapulted her onto the global stage. After becoming an official Angel in 2010, the model was featured in ad campaigns for Tom Ford and Versace, and walked for the likes of Oscar de la Renta, Tom Ford, Chanel and Fendi. She was chosen to wear the Fantasy Bra in 2013 and appeared on four Vogue covers the following year. As of 2017, Swanepoel is the Angel with the largest following on Instagram, with 11.4 million followers. In 2016, Swanepoel announced that she and long-time boyfriend Hermann Nicoli, whom she met in Paris when she was 17, were expecting their first child, Anacã. The model is an avid supporter of Mothers2Mothers, a charity working towards reaching an “HIV-free generation” of children and mothers in Africa. 2017 marks her return on the VS runway. To prepare, the South African model has been practicing a combination of yoga, pilates and resistance training. Her secret weapon? An energy-boosting breakfast smoothie, combining banana, berries, almond butter, protein powder, chia seeds and coconut water. column1: Adriana Lima: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Name: Adriana Lima Age: 36 Nationality: Brazilian Height: 5'10'' VS shows to date: 17 Adriana Lima is the longest-serving Victoria's Secret Angel of all time. She signed her contract in 2000, only a year after her debut on the VS runway. Since then, she has opened the show five times and worn the Fantasy Bra three times, in 2008, 2010 and 2014. Born in Salvador, Brazil, Lima started modelling in her early teens, after winning the Ford agency's Supermodel of Brazil contest aged 15. She then moved to New York and signed with Elite Model Management, walking for Anna Sui and Philosophy as early as 1998. View Gallery 3 Photos Adriana Lima: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile Since then, the Brazilian supermodel has added a long list of names to her catwalk portfolio including Alexander McQueen, Balmain, Givenchy, Louis Vuitton and Calvin Klein, in addition to advertising contracts with Maybelline, Sportmax, Marc Jacobs and IWC Watches. In 2016, she was the second highest-paid model in the world, according to Forbes. She is currently the most social Angel, with 20.5 million followers across Instagram, Facebook and Twitter. Lima has walked every Victoria's Secret show since 1999, with the exception of 2009, because of her first pregnancy. In 2012, she wore her Angel wings only five weeks after giving birth to her second daughter. She credits her figure to boxing—her favourite workout since the age of 19—which she supplements with daily rope-skipping sessions in preparation for the annual VS show. Her only vice? Chocolate molten cake. column1: Karlie Kloss: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Name: Karlie Kloss Age: 25 Nationality: American Height: 5'11'' VS shows to date: 4 Karlie Kloss was the first model to become a Victoria's Secret Angel the same year of her debut for the annual Fashion Show, in 2011. She's making her return to the VS runway this year, after briefly parting from the brand in 2015 to attend New York University. A successful entrepreneur, Kloss manages a number of projects on the side: She has created a line of vegan, gluten-free cookies with Momofuku Milk Bar, dubbed Karlie's Kookies; has launched Kode with Klossy, a scholarship programme for girls interested in learning how to code; and her YouTube channel, Klossy, founded in 2015, has more than half a million subscribers. View Gallery 4 Photos Karlie Kloss: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show 2017 – Model Profile The Chicago-born supermodel was discovered, aged 13, at a charity fashion show organised in a mall in St. Louis, Missouri. In 2006, after seeing her pictures in a local magazine, Elite Model Management New York decided to offer her a contract. Shortly after, Kloss got her first big job - a campaign by Bruce Weber for Abercrombie Kids, and, in 2008, she had her real breakthrough, booking 64 shows. A veteran of the catwalk, her characteristic walk has been described by Vogue as “the most alluring and slinkiest on the runway”. In 2009, Kloss was chosen as the face of Marc Jacobs's new fragrance, Lola, and over the years she has appeared in campaigns for Gap, Topshop, Alexander McQueen, Bulgari, Dior and Hermès. Her fame extends well beyond fashion: She made a cameo as herself in cult teen-drama Gossip Girl in 2010; has hosted the red carpet at the 2013 MTV Movie Awards pre-show; and, more recently, has made an appearance in friend Taylor Swift's Bad Blood music video and on the stage of her 1989 World Tour. Kloss grew up studying ballet, which helped her gain control of her body rhythm and muscles “the most valuable thing” she could have done to prepare herself for modelling. She tries to work out every day, combining different exercises including pilates, spinning and running. Her food obsessions include kale chips, almond butter, avocado and dark chocolate. column1: 20 designer wedding wear options that are perfect for a mature bride
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Don't compromise on style View Gallery 20 Photos 20 outfit ideas that are perfect for a mature bride With most Indian designers catering to the needs of young brides and stores brimming with millennial trends, it can be a difficult task for a mature bride to find the perfect outfit for her wedding. If you are one of them, take heart; we have put together an edit of the best pieces, whatever your needs. Truth to be told—age is just a number. You can be 40 and pull off an off-shoulder blouse with ease, or be 25 with a preference for modest fashion. Whatever your reason, if you find yourself looking for a more mature aesthetic, there's still a lot to choose from. Being on trend is not a bad idea, but don't fall prey to styles that won't suit your body type. Have a clear vision of the kind of bride you want to be and shop accordingly. Be mindful of the choice of the fabrics. Turn to softer silks and georgette for a more figure flattering effect. Opt for comfortable separates like shararas and floor-grazing anarkalis for the mehandi and haldi events. Both are easy to dress up and comfortable enough to survive the long nights in (minus the weight of an embellished lehenga). For the pheras, a traditional wedding sari is a fail-safe option, but don't rule out a designer lehenga just because you don't want your midriff on display. Simply swap the trendier small cholis for a longer blouse, or pick an opaque dupatta to drape over your outfit. If you don't want the hassle of separates, choose an embellished dress instead. Choose an element to focus on and do it well. If you are opting for a bold colour, go easy on the embellishment and vice versa. Scroll through our slideshow for our top picks for a mature bride. column1: Careers in fashion: Gaurav Gupta on making avant-garde designs commercial
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion And the importance of having a business strategy Designer Gaurav Gupta can easily be touted as a pioneer of the new wave of contemporary Indian fashion. Ever since his runway debut in 2006, Gupta has always led the conversation on reinventing conventional fashion with his commitment to his distinct design DNA. Gupta debuted his first collection after his return from Central Saint Martins in London, replete with strong military influences. During the initial years, his approach was considered by many as too severe, but that did not deter him from continuing down this less-travelled path. With every passing collection, Gupta strengthened his position as a designer who had his heart fixed on marrying the conceptual with the classic, and the avant-garde with the commercially appealing. His 3D embroideries, volume play, extempore draping and futuristic construction are now brand signatures, sought-after by brides and celebrities alike. What's noteworthy is that this engineered edge comes from inspirations that are more whimsical in nature, making it a beautiful merging of contrasts. “I am inspired by almost everything. My main inspiration comes from nature, forest, sky, water, shape, form, art, architecture, and thought. It is almost mostly abstract, something fantastical.” Over the years, Gupta's brand repertoire has grown to include womenswear couture, semi-couture and western wear. Gupta has also partnered with Swarovski for a line of jewellery in 2010, with Mawi in 2014, and with Klove Studios for a lighting collection this year. The launch of his first limited-edition scent called ‘Again' also took place this year, as did his collaboration with New York-based footwear designer Chloe Gosselin. Cementing his futuristic approach, Gupta recently associated with IBM's Artificial Intelligence platform, Watson, wherein he created a cognitive sari gown integrated with lights that changes colours and patterns based on the personality of the person interacting with the wearer of the gown (worn by Archie Punjabi at the Vogue Women of the Year Awards 2017). Vogue spoke to the designer about keeping it cutting-edge in an industry that is cutthroat. When you started out in 2004, your work was considered unconventional for the Indian market. What was your vision back then? From then to now, my vision continues to be about making artistic, unconventional fashion a reality in the Indian market. The brand has always been experimental, out-of-the-box and at the same time sophisticated. Having said that, over the years the brand and me have both evolved—there is a deeper understanding of how the business of fashion works, and how my brand is positioned in the market. It is always a balance between art and commerce. We have gained confidence with each passing year. Your label is a go-to for modern Indian women who are on the lookout for non-tradition cocktail and wedding wear. Did you consciously decide to shift focus to this audience? It was a natural progression. We started doing couture around the same time as my brother's wedding. Soon after, couture shows started taking place and the collections happened. There was this moment in 2007 when I realised that I am in India, and I just cannot ignore the market here. That was when we started making sari gowns, for which we received a great commercial response. It was interesting to pioneer an ensemble like this, and to discover that there was indeed a big gap in the market for it. Today, we are making bespoke couture gowns for the clients across the country and internationally, and are also pushing boundaries of what can be defined as Indian wear and Indo-western wear. We are also on the brink of launching our cocktail menswear line. View Gallery 38 Photos Gaurav Gupta at Amazon India Fashion Week Autumn/Winter 2016 Gaurav Gupta at Amazon India Fashion Week autumn/winter 2016 How important is it for a couture brand to cater to the wedding market in India? How can you do so without compromising on your core aesthetic? The couture market in India is 95 per cent of the wedding market. We are very lucky to have a cultural wedding market that is so exuberant. India is one of the few places in the world where the couture market exists on such a large scale. The couture brands largely exist only because of the wedding market. Talking about myself, I have not followed any rules, but made my own. We stay true to the times we live in—we are fortunate that our patrons believe in our inimitable design language. This has only grown exponentially, and this demand for a change of aesthetic was long overdue. Your brand now has top of mind recall when it comes to cocktail wear. How did you reach this stage of commercial viability and popularity? Our cocktail wear still continues to be very avant-garde with its detailing. But to achieve commercial success, it is important for a fashion brand to have a well-chalked-out business strategy to zero in on what is working for them, to have a solid business partner (which in my case is my brother Saurabh Gupta), to learn to strategise, and to have a solid commercial plan. Young designers don't have a business strategy, and are scared to deal with finances and money. Coming from a business family, I'm not scared of talking money. It's also about striking a balance between profitability and creativity. You launched your first line of perfumes this month. Was it a conscious strategy to expand your product line? What comes next? Yes, we have been working on it for the past four years, but the process has been completely organic. Jahnvi (Lakhota Nandan of The Perfume Library) and I have been friends for 12 years, since the beginning of our brands. We have shared some really beautiful design dialogues, and it was our passion for abstract and beautiful things that has resulted in this perfume. Taking up the challenge of entering the new and nascent industry of perfumery in India was a great way for our brand to expand. Next, we are launching menswear with sexy, avant-garde tuxedoes, so that grooms can keep up with their stylish brides. View Gallery 54 Photos Gaurav Gupta at India Couture Week 2016 Gaurav Gupta at India Couture Week 2016 What was your first ever runway show, and what were your learnings from it? Which are your top three runway shows till date? It was my NIFT graduate show, and I was just amazed that I could finish the collection in time! The collection was called ‘Alastor', which is a Greek mythological character. The show served as the foundation for what was to come. My key learning was that hard work always pays off, as I also won some awards in Japan for the collection. Among the top three shows would be ‘Lightfall', our couture 2013 show with which we defined our identity in the couture market. Another would be our Lakmé Fashion Week Finale show in 2015 with the collection ‘Sculpt', as it was an amazing balance between conceptual and wearable global appeal. I would also choose my most recent couture show for the ‘Moondust' collection as it was purely magical. At what point did you realise you were going from a relatively known label to one that was recognised all across the country? I think I'm still realising that. An incident from about six years ago comes to mind, when a few engineering students wanted to collaborate with us and invest in our company. I think it was special because this response was from those who were not even a part of the fashion ecosystem. The fact that they were well-versed with my work made me realise that we were becoming a household name. View Gallery 58 Photos Gaurav Gupta at India Couture Week 2017 Gaurav Gupta at India Couture Week 2016 Did you have a mentor when you started out? Yes, my father and my brother. I also bounce ideas off my closest friends, especially Navkirat Sodhi and Vijendra Bhardwaj. What is one ensemble you've created that you are most proud of? It is the iconic Lightfall gown, which has been worn by the likes of Deepika Padukone at global events. It eventually became synonymous with the identity of the brand—conceptual meets sexy, and has been ordered by several brides as well. What is your advice to the new crop of designers who have an avant-garde design sensibility but still want it to be a profitable business? Definitely have a business plan in place, put down numbers for the next three years, if not five. Find your own identity and never forget that originality goes a long way. column1: From Deepika Padukone to Sonam Kapoor, everyone is wearing these earrings
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion And why its here to stay Put your inner minimalist to sleep, this is no place for her to be. Statement earrings are back to ruling the runways—and our jewellery kits—and this season, they come strictly in XXL, with a heavy dose of fringe on the side. Behold, the maximalist tassel earrings that everyone from Bollywood celebrities to the cool crew of street style have fallen head over heels for. You probably noticed this statement style first putting in a bold appearance with Deepika Padukone, soaking up the spotlight alongside the star's international red carpet debut at the MTV EMAs 2016. Decked in standout separates from Monisha Jaising, Padukone went in for the kill with shoulder-grazing tassels from Valliyan. The rest is history, of the headline-making kind. Borrow from the best When in doubt, look to Bollywood's cool kids to decode trends for you. After Padukone gave the trend her stamp of approval, new mom Kareena Kapoor Khan went print-on-print in Missoni separates with turquoise tassels dusting her collarbone, courtesy Valliyan. Sonam Kapoor elevated a basic traditional look by coordinating her tasseled Rashmi Verma dupatta with similar fringed earrings. If you're looking to break free of the pack, take notes from Shraddha Kapoor who gave hers a metallic update. View Gallery 8 Photos Deepika to Kareena, everyone is in love with this earring trend – celebrities Wear it right Once you've found a pair as vibrant as your personality in the right length—we personally believe shoulder-grazing or nothing—let your tasseled add-ons have their moment fair and square in the spotlight by opting for a pulled-back hairstyle. These conversation-starters come in all vivid hues of the rainbow, which makes them the perfect pick-me-up for when the winter blues hit. However, the main allure of this trend perhaps lies in the fact that they are incredibly DIY-friendly, so if you've binged on Stranger Things 2 twice already and don't quite know what to do with your free time, feel free to let your creative side take over and craft your very own statement-making pair. What you definitely shouldn't do Take heed; the more-is-more vibe of this trend means that you could easily end up on the wrong side of maximalist fashion if you don't take caution. If you're looking to coordinate your tassels precisely with your outfit, ensure that you work in another colour in the final look, either by way of shoes or a belt to break the monotony. If your tasseled pair crosses the collarbone in terms of length, it's advisable to take a rain check on necklaces altogether to avoid diverting attention. Whether it's at a sun-kissed beach in Hawaii or your weekly brunch with the girls, if you're looking to work this statement style, pick from our edit of the hottest pieces of the season. column1: Virat Kohli on collaborating with Puma for his new line, One8
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion And the secret behind the name Between making news with his victories on the pitch and holidaying with Anushka Sharma, Virat Kohli has been working on launching his very own fashion label. On November 9, the cricketer announced the launch of One8 (the name is inspired by his jersey number, 18), created in collaboration with Puma, at Select City Walk, Delhi. The brand features a collection of active wear separates ranging from sweatshirts to logo tees. At the launch event, the cricketer let us in on his experience. "It is very exciting for me," said Kohli. "The main aim of doing an athleisure line is to bring style into sports, so that people can feel comfortable in fashionable clothes," he revealed. The line draws from Kohli's personal sense of style—think comfortable jackets, relaxed T-shirts and trousers in easy fabrics—with a palette of black, grey, white and olive. We spoke to him on what went into the making of One8. On the journey of creating: "It's a very special feeling. Six months ago I had my very first interaction with Puma and now the line is ready. All the things that were decided back then have come alive." On the campaign: "The tag line for our collaboration is “Come Out and Play”. The idea is to get people to be physically active. I wanted to create the kind of clothes that are fashionable and at the same time make it easy for people to take part in physical activities.” On his personal style: “People have to force me to wear formal clothes, that's how I dress up. I love wearing casual, comfortable clothes. I don't like anything that's flashy. When we started this process, the Puma team just opened my suitcase and saw what kind of clothes that were there in my bag. They took inspiration from there and incorporated those colours (I was very particular about that) and style.” On the one thing he could wear his entire life: “It will have to be a pair of grey track pants that are super comfortable, a matching grey T-shirt and white sneakers. Grey on grey with white is my go-to look.” On his favourite pieces from the collection: “The first one is this comfortable black T-shirt that says “Unapologetically Me”. I love it because it exactly describes the person I am. I don't like body-hugging clothes and this one is very loose and comfortable. Then the second one is plain black high-low T-shirt and also the olive-green tank top because it's my favourite colour and you can wear it under a jacket too.” One the three things he can never leave home without: “My phone, my sunglasses, and music is very important for me so my headphones and my ear plugs.” The price for the collection ranges from Rs 1,499 to Rs 4,000. column1: Daily style directory: 13/11/2017
column2: © Vogue Images Fashion Classic hues versus jewel tones View Gallery 25 Photos Daily style directory: 13/11/2017 Intense, festive hues had a huge moment in celebrity wardrobes this weekend. Kajol made a rare public appearance in Kolkata wearing a regal green and gold Sabyasachi sari, while Vaani Kapoor went all-out in a gold Falguni Shane Peacock gown. Both Neha Dhupia and Diana Penty picked midnight blues (the former in an anarkali jacket, the latter in an Anita Dongre lehenga), and Anushka Sharma accompanied beau Virat Kohli at a sports event in a scarlet Nikhil Thampi suit. Red was a favourite overseas as well, with Jessica Chastain picking a fiery Alexander McQueen ensemble in LA, and Naomi Campbell glittering at a New York gala in an asymmetric Monse gown.
